episode.title: Pyroclastic Flow Engulfing the Bay of Naples

synopsis: A vast pyroclastic flow erupts from Mount Vesuvius, rapidly spreading across the entire Bay of Naples, engulfing coastal cities and harbor structures under a lethal cloud of ash and gas.

caption:
A massive pyroclastic flow erupts from Mount Vesuvius, rapidly spreading across the entire Bay of Naples, Italy.

This impossible flow covers an area of over 100 square kilometers within seconds, reaching speeds of 500 km/h and engulfing coastal cities and harbor moles under a lethal cloud of ash and gas.

Pyroclastic flows are deadly, fast-moving currents of hot gas and volcanic debris. The 79 AD eruption of Vesuvius buried Pompeii and Herculaneum, with flows extending a few tens of kilometers. A similar devastating eruption occurred in 1631.

While devastating, even the largest historical pyroclastic flows are confined by topography and dissipate energy over distance. For a flow to cover an entire bay, it would require an eruption column and energy release orders of magnitude greater than any known supervolcanic event, defying conservation of mass and energy for the Earth's scale.

This is a simulation, not real footage.

Could any human structure withstand the force of such a flow?
